Sutcliffe No More is the follow-up name for the band known as Sutcliffe Jugend. It was founded by Kevin Tomkins in 1982. It started as a Power Electronics act, quickly gaining a name for itself, before branching out stylistically, creating a distinctive style that drew influence from all manner of genres while keeping true to their roots as a noise act. In its original form Sutcliffe Jugend existed for less than a year before Tomkins stopped the project to join Whitehouse. He reformed the group in 1994 with Paul Taylor who also played on some of the project’s early material. The project ended in 2019. They released one album under a new name, Slaves No More, then continued as Sutcliffe No More.

Control is Thomas Garrison from Santa Cruz who works as a branding / body modification artist and as a mastering engineer at his own Misanthrope Studio and has also initiated the Industrial / Ambient project Exsanguinate. He made a name as one of the finest American Power Electronics acts since the end of the nineties with a multitude of releases and highly regarded live performances in Europe and the U.S..

Kommando was Dan Courtman’s pre-Thorofon project which released two cassette tapes and two cds during its initial existence. Four years after the ‚Crimefactory‘ album Kommando was re-established and has releases several albums and singles since then.

Bragolin is a Dutch dark wave/post-punk project led by Edwin van der Velde, known for its strong melodic hooks present on gothic dance floors worldwide. Drawing from ’80s Bass VI lines, ’60s and ’70s organs, and ’90s shoegaze guitars, Bragolin blends vintage and modern elements into a sound inspired by post-apocalyptic and horror cinema. The project takes its name from Italian painter Giovanni Bragolin, famed for his “Crying Boy” paintings.

The debut album I Saw Nothing Good So I Left (2018) featured the track Into Those Woods, which is now a modern- day dance floor classic. The song surpassed 10 million all-time streams in 2025, establishing Bragolin as a consistent presence within the global dark wave and gothic scene. In 2019, van der Velde collaborated with fellow Dutch artist Adam Tristar on the second album Let Out The Noise Inside, which leaned further into electronic and synth-based production.

In 2026, Bragolin releases the new album I Don’t Like What It Does To Me, unfolding in gradually revealed chapters. Building on the project’s signature sound, the record combines Bass VI melodies, organ lines, and rich atmospheric production. Field recordings, synthetic ocean textures, water-phones, and experimental sound sources create a layered, immersive listening experience. The album features Feel This Flame Unfold, a duet with dark wave artist Carrellee.

Carrellee overlays delicately sensual vocals over a wall of scorched synths and processed tapes. She had some help crafting her noir synth-pop sound from co-producer Brett Bullion (Low, Poliça, Bad Bad Hats.) Carrellee turned to the microKORG and Yamaha DX7 synths after finding the folk music she had been doing to fall a bit flat in expressing the intensity of the year, including going through a divorce with her personal and musical partner.

Process Party and Effetto Notte join forces to launch HALL OF BATS, a new collaborative event series dedicated to darkwave, minimal synth, deathrock, post-punk and the darker corners of electronic music.

For its first edition, we bring three live acts to Urban Spree, followed by an afterparty until late.

LOVATARAXX — FR

Headlining the first Hall of Bats are Lovataraxx, a French duo originally from Grenoble and currently based in Lyon.

Their sound dives into coldwave, minimal synth and dark electronic music through corrosive synthesizers, sharp drum machines, hypnotic voices and a strong post-punk energy.

With more than 500 shows across Europe and America over the past decade, Lovataraxx have developed an intense and highly dynamic live presence. Their albums Hébéphrénie and Sophomore explore a universe of impulsive beats, haunting synth melodies and sounds that feel simultaneously strange and familiar.

Bandcamp:  
[https://lovataraxx.bandcamp.com/]

HYSTERIC HELEN — SK

Hysteric Helen is a darkwave and deathrock project from Bratislava, Slovakia.

Their sound channels the atmospheric tension and driving rhythms of 1980s post-punk, deathrock and batcave aesthetics. Raw DIY production, haunting melodies and a strong underground attitude shape their distinctly gothic sound.

Bandcamp:  
[https://hysterichelen.bandcamp.com/](

OLGHA — IT / PL

Olgha is a one-person Italian-Polish project combining the melancholic elements of minimal synth-pop with darkwave.

Melting nostalgia for the past with a search for contemporary sounds, Olgha moves between minimal electronics, melancholy and dark synth-pop, with a strong DIY approach.

SPK are one of the founding names of industrial music. Formed in Sydney in 1978 by Graeme Revell and Neil Hill, the group helped redefine the possibilities of experimental sound, combining electronic music, noise, ritual, performance art and political provocation into a body of work whose influence continues to resonate across industrial, electronic and extreme music today.

Albums such as Information Overload Unit, Leichenschrei, Auto-Da-Fé and the visionary Zamia Lehmanni established SPK as one of the most innovative and uncompromising acts of the post-industrial era. Their work pushed beyond conventional song structures, fusing machine rhythms, orchestral textures, non-Western instrumentation and cinematic atmosphere years before such approaches became commonplace.

Following SPK's final performances in the late 1980s, Graeme Revell went on to become one of Hollywood's most celebrated film composers, scoring over one hundred feature films and games, including The Crow, The Craft, From Dusk Till Dawn, Sin City, Blow, Call of Duty and Dune.

In 2026, after an absence of almost forty years from the touring circuit, SPK returns to Europe with an entirely new live production. Joined by Robert Revell, Graeme Revell brings SPK's pioneering legacy into the present, combining the group's original spirit of experimentation with cutting-edge digital technologies, immersive visuals and a powerful new sonic architecture. This is not a reunion driven by nostalgia, but the next chapter in one of industrial music's most influential and uncompromising artistic journeys.

Alvar is your fear, bad mood and the knife in your heart.

Berlin-based project TWIN NOIR transforms analog rawness into urban ecstasy. Somewhere between alternative, electro, and modern post-punk elements, they create a sound that gets under your skin. Driving rhythms, striking guitars, and melancholic tones merge into a distinctive style. Minimalist German-language lyrics explore themes that give their music emotional depth.

Following tours across Europe, the UK, the Balkans, and Mexico, and support shows for DAF, She Past Away, and Men Without Hats, TWIN NOIR have built a growing international reputation. They have appeared at festivals such as Extramuralhas Festival, Summerside Festival, and Amphi Festival and were featured multiple times by Iggy Pop on Iggy Confidential on BBC Radio 6.

With their new album “Chapter III”, released via the Berlin label Odyssey Music Network, TWIN NOIR are heading out on an extensive tour across Germany and Europe. Known for their electrifying live shows, TWIN NOIR impress with energetic performances and a danceable sound. Inspired by Berlin’s club culture, punk, and vaudeville, their shows celebrate freedom, creativity, and art, creating an irresistible pull. Made for dark dancefloors and festival stages alike and for those who appreciate intense concerts where you can let go and fully immerse yourself.�

Hinfort is a solo project from Cologne that will regularly release dark, melancholic music in the style of post-punk and dark wave starting in October 2024. Its hallmarks are emotional lyrics about isolation and inner darkness, supported by atmospheric, often minimalist soundscapes.

Girls Under Glass wurden 1986 in Hamburg gegründet – in einer Zeit tiefgreifender gesellschaftspolitischer Umbrüche, aber jenseits klar definierter musikalischer Szenen.

Während Gothic und Dark Wave Ende der 1980er zunehmend stilistische Konventionen entwickelten, verfolgte die Band von Beginn an einen eigenständigen Ansatz: dunkel, experimentell, emotional – aber ohne Genreklischees.

Gegründet von Sänger Tom Lücke, Keyboarder Hauke Harms und Gitarrist Volker Zacharias, entwickelten Girls Under Glass früh eine unverwechselbare Klangsprache, die sich eher aus Einflüssen wie 80er-Wave, frühem Post-Punk und experimenteller dunkler Elektronik speiste als aus dem klassischen Gothic-Kanon. Bereits die frühen Veröffentlichungen – darunter die Alben Humus (1988) und Flowers (1989) – machten deutlich, dass einfache Zuschreibungen hier nicht greifen würden.

Nach dem Ausstieg von Tom Lücke 1990 übernahm Volker Zacharias Gesang und Songwriting und prägte den Sound der Band nachhaltig. Mit dem von Rodney Orpheus (The Cassandra Complex) produzierten Album Positive (1991) etablierten Girls Under Glass ihre bis heute zentrale Stärke: außergewöhnliches Songwriting, das atmosphärische Tiefe, Melodie und stilistische Offenheit miteinander verbindet. Die folgenden Alben (Darius, Christus, Crystals & Stones) führten diese Entwicklung konsequent fort, ohne sich zu wiederholen.

Auch stilistische Ausbrüche – etwa das gitarrenlastigere Firewalker (1997) – waren stets Teil eines künstlerischen Prozesses, der Veränderung nicht als Risiko, sondern als Notwendigkeit verstand. Mit Equilibrium (1999), Minddiver (2001) und Zyklus (2004) fand die Band erneut zu einem fokussierten, vielschichtigen Sound zurück, der auch frühe Einflüsse wieder zuließ. Nach längerer kreativer Pause und weiteren personellen Veränderungen meldeten sich Girls Under Glass schließlich eindrucksvoll mit dem Album Backdraft (2023) zurück – ein Werk, das zeigt, dass kreative Relevanz kein Verfallsdatum kennt.

Nach dem Jubiläumsjahr 2026 schlagen Girls Under Glass 2027 ein weiteres Kapitel auf: Clubtour zum neuen Album!

In den letzten 20 Jahren spielten Girls Under Glass nur eine Handvoll Clubkonzerte. Genau diese unmittelbare Nähe zwischen Band und Publikum wollen sie nun bewusst wieder aufleben lassen.

Die Clubtour 2027 bietet eine der wenigen Gelegenheiten, Girls Under Glass in einem intimen Rahmen zu erleben – nahbar, intensiv und jenseits großer Bühnenroutinen.

Für langjährige Fans wie auch für neue Hörer:innen ist diese Tour mehr als Nostalgie: Sie ist eine Einladung zu einer gemeinsamen, unmittelbaren und intimen Live-Erfahrung gemeinsam einer Band, die sich über 40 Jahre hinweg immer wieder neu erfunden hat – ohne ihren eigenen Kern jemals zu verlieren. Präsentiert werden neben den bekannten Klassikern und Live-Highlights auch Songs aus dem neuen Album, welches im Frühjahr 2027 via Dependent Records erscheinen wird.
